- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Easter Vigil is a significant service in the Catholic Church that marks the pinnacle of the Easter Triduum.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Easter Vigil typically lasts around 2-3 hours.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The service begins in darkness, symbolizing the darkness of sin and the tomb, and features the lighting of the Paschal candle.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The service includes a series of readings from the Old and New Testaments, music, Baptism, Confirmation, and the Eucharist.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The congregation is invited to renew their baptismal vows during the service.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Holy Saturday is a day of waiting, silence, and anticipation in the Catholic tradition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Harrowing of Hell refers to Jesus' descent into the realm of the dead to free the souls of the righteous.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Harrowing of Hell is represented in Catholic art and literature, including frescoes, illuminated manuscripts, and works by Dante Alighieri.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Paschal candle symbolizes Christ's light, presence, victory over death, and eternal life.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Paschal candle is lit during the Easter Vigil and remains in the church throughout the Easter season.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Easter Vigil service differs from the Easter Sunday Mass in its structure, length, and the specific rituals performed, including the Baptism and Confirmation of new members.
